Customer to provide sample traffic profile and data sensitivity matrix

header: Date: 2026-03-31 | Time: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 52 min | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Park (CSM); Rajiv Menon (CTO), Emily Torres (Head of ML), Samir Khan (Platform Eng), Laura Benson (Security)
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick roll call?
00:06 Rajiv Menon: Rajiv here. hi Maya.
00:08 Emily Torres: Emily — good to be here.
00:10 Samir Khan: Samir on platform.
00:12 Laura Benson: Laura, security.
00:14 Maya Chen: awesome. Omar from our SE team will run through the technical plan and sizing. Jules is here for the account stuff. goal for the hour is to confirm success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan and timeline for the POC. sound good?
00:28 Rajiv Menon: yes that sounds right.
00:30 Omar Patel: great, uh I'll tee off — give high level of what we recommend and then dive into integration options — SDKs, openai-compatible endpoints, and specifically function/tool calling and structured output because Emily mentioned structured JSON outputs in the RFP.
00:44 Emily Torres: correct — the main driver is automated extraction of key entities from customer support transcripts and then a downstream rules engine needs strict JSON, so hallucination tolerance is low.
00:55 Omar Patel: understood. starting with success criteria — typical POC success items we see: 1) correctness: accuracy of structured extraction vs labeled dataset, target F1 >= 0.85; 2) latency: p95 generation latency under 700ms for single-turn calls on hosted mode or under 200ms on dedicated for short prompts; 3) throughput: sustain 120 qps bursty with tail smoothing via batching; 4) cost estimates within X of their current budget — we'll model tokens. are those aligned with what you had in mind?
01:20 Emily Torres: accuracy target sounds right. latency numbers are acceptable but we need to confirm what "short prompts" means — our average is 350 tokens per request (includes context) and we have some longer 2k token cases.
01:33 Samir Khan: and for throughput that's concurrent requests, right? we're expecting about 3k requests per minute during peak which is about 50 rps sustained and 200 rps burst.
01:44 Omar Patel: thanks, that clarifies. we'll model both median prompt (350 tokens) and long prompt (2k tokens). for baseline benchmarking we'll run three profiles: short (<=400 tokens), medium (400-1200), long (1200-2k). recommended bench targets: p95 latency short <700ms on Redwood Hosted with our recommended batching/kv cache, and for Dedicated you'd see p95 under 250ms.
02:08 Rajiv Menon: curious about caching — you guys do prefix caching and KV cache for chat, right? how much can that reduce tokens and latency?
02:16 Omar Patel: yes we do automatic prefix and KV caching. depends on reuse — for support transcripts reuse rate is moderate because user context changes, but for system prompts and templated instructions you see 15-35% token savings often. note: KV cache helps with cost and latency on long-chat scenarios, but on single-turn extraction it's less, unless you have repeated tokens.
02:36 Emily Torres: benchmark methodology — can you share the scripts? we want reproducible runs.
02:40 Omar Patel: absolutely — we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet and a dockerized harness that hits our OpenAI-compatible endpoint and our native SDKs. I'll put the repo link in the follow up.
02:50 Maya Chen: quick stop — on integration patterns: Atlas prefers OpenAI-compatible endpoints for quicker dev integration. do you support function calling and structured output in the OpenAI-compatible path?
02:59 Omar Patel: yes, we surface an OpenAI-compatible v1/chat/completions endpoint and function-calling semantics. slight caveat: advanced function/tool orchestration and multi-step tool calling we recommend using our native SDK where we provide richer helpers; but for basic function schemas and strict JSON you can use the compatible endpoint with the same function_schema param. sometimes the auto-parser mislabels KV cache as K V cache in transcripts but the runtime supports the same features.
03:25 Samir Khan: and SDK languages? we prefer Python and Node.
03:28 Omar Patel: official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. we also have REST examples and a lightweight JS wrapper for browser contexts.
03:35 Laura Benson: security — we need encryption at rest, KMS integration, SOC 2 and an audit trail for every request. can you meet that for a POC?
03:43 Maya Chen: yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs. for POC we can offer dedicated test tenancy with logs and a SOC 2 report. for production we can discuss Private deployment.
03:54 Laura Benson: ok. also need SSO (SAML) and RBAC for the console.
03:58 Jules Park: we can enable SAML SSO for your org and show RBAC roles in the Console demo.
04:05 Rajiv Menon: network — can we do VPC peering or private link?
04:08 Omar Patel: yes, both. for dedicated POCs we typically do VPC peering and a small NAT gateway config. Samir, we heard you'll open a peering ticket?
04:17 Samir Khan: yep I'll start that and share VPC CIDR constraints.
04:20 Omar Patel: great. now on workload sizing — you mentioned 3k rpm with avg 350 tokens. so per minute that’s roughly 1M tokens/min? wait let me recalc — 3k requests * 350 tokens = 1,050,000 tokens per minute, which is about 63M tokens per hour during peak. does that match your ops numbers?
04:40 Emily Torres: that math is close; our real average across days is lower but peaks hit that. also embeddings for search are another workload — roughly 10k docs re-embedding monthly, and realtime embedding calls at 30 rps during search spikes.
04:54 Omar Patel: ok we'll scope two parallel POC workloads: 1) extraction (generation + function call), 2) embeddings for search. bench plan will include token-per-second tuning, batching policy, and quantization profiles for Dedicated.
05:05 Maya Chen: timeline — recommended POC length?
05:08 Omar Patel: 4 weeks typical: week 0 (prep & access), week 1 (baseline single-node runs, smoke tests), week 2 (full benchmark runs across short/medium/long), week 3 (integration and accuracy labeling, running labeled evals), week 4 (wrap-up, findings and SOW). you can compress to 3 if you provide labeled data earlier.
05:26 Rajiv Menon: we can commit to 3 if we get the harness early.
05:30 Maya Chen: commercial ask — do you need a deposit or trial credits?
05:33 Jules Park: for POC we can open a free trial with limited credits; for Dedicated test tenancy we typically ask for a short commitment or refundable deposit — I'll include options in the costing.
05:43 Emily Torres: function calling reliability — do you provide deterministic JSON mode to avoid hallucinations?
05:48 Omar Patel: we support strict schema enforcement where the model is asked to output only JSON matching a schema; we also run a lightweight post-parse checker in-line. for high-assurance workloads we recommend function calling with validation in your app layer and Redwood's structured-output flag.
06:03 Samir Khan: about metrics — we'd like token-level cost, per-route latency, and traceable request IDs to map back to our logs.
06:12 Maya Chen: yes, Console exposes token-level breakdowns, per-model dashboards, trace links. we can forward request IDs as a header and show them in traces.
06:20 Laura Benson: data retention — for POC we need to ensure logs are retained 30 days and then auto-purged. can you set retention windows?
06:29 Jules Park: retention policies configurable at the project level; we can set 30-day retention for the POC and provide a data deletion proof.
06:37 Omar Patel: ok moving into integration planning specifics: for your dev team we recommend starting with the OpenAI-compatible endpoints to minimize code changes. examples: chat completions with functions, plus an embeddings endpoint. for Python we recommend the redwood-sdk which provides a wrapper that maps one-to-one to openai parameters but adds helpers for streaming and structured parsing.
06:58 Emily Torres: do you support streaming for function responses? some of our consumers are streaming-first.
07:02 Omar Patel: streaming is supported in both compatible and native SDKs. caveat: streaming structured JSON requires reassembly and final validation — we provide helpers in the SDK to do that safely.
07:14 Rajiv Menon: bench infra — will you run the tests from your region or should we run from our VPC?
07:19 Omar Patel: both options; usually we run an external benchmark to simulate production latency, and we recommend you run a couple runs from your VPC to capture egress and peering impacts. we'll provide the harness and a reproducible script.
07:30 Emily Torres: for embeddings quality we want recall@10 > 0.75 on our eval set. is that realistic with your recommended models?
07:38 Omar Patel: likely yes — we'll propose a model lineup and quantization options. if results differ we can try different open models in the catalog.
07:45 Samir Khan: about costs — can you give a preliminary cost per million tokens for hosted versus dedicated?
07:52 Jules Park: preliminary numbers: hosted approx $X per million (we'll put actual numbers in the deck) and Dedicated nominally lower at scale with reserved commits. I'll include a cost sheet in the follow up.
08:03 Maya Chen: small note: sometimes the transcript engine mis-hears 'Redwood Dedicated' as 'Redwood Dedicate' in our internal notes — ignore that.
08:08 (laughter)
08:10 Laura Benson: compliance docs — we'll need SOC 2 Type II and encryption attestations.
08:14 Jules Park: we'll attach SOC 2 and our redacted audit in the follow up.
08:18 Omar Patel: integration checklist summary: 1) grant API access and test keys 2) share sample prompts and label set 3) run baseline harness on short/med/long 4) run embedding recall tests 5) validate structured output and function calling with your downstream rules engine.
08:35 Rajiv Menon: that helps. on a technical note — are there any special headers or request IDs you require?
08:40 Omar Patel: no required headers besides auth, but we support x-request-id to be submitted back in traces. we also support a customer_id header for tenant tagging.
08:48 Emily Torres: what's the rollback or fallback strategy if a model degrades during the POC?
08:51 Omar Patel: we have auto-fallback to a compatible smaller model and a canary rollout option; also you can pin model versions. for POC we'll propose a 2-model plan: a higher-accuracy variant and a cheaper variant for cost comparisons.
09:06 Maya Chen: ok let's capture next steps and owners. (brief pause) Omar, can you bullet the benchmark plan in the follow up?
09:14 Omar Patel: yes — I'll share: test harness repo, spreadsheet with token distributions, target metrics, and a one-click script to run the 3-profile set.
09:22 Maya Chen: Jules will share pricing and SOW options.
09:25 Jules Park: yup.
09:26 Rajiv Menon: Emily and Samir will prep the sample dataset and traffic profile.
09:30 Emily Torres: will do.
09:32 Maya Chen: any other questions before we wrap?
09:34 Laura Benson: timeline for documents?
09:36 Jules Park: we'll send benchmark materials and SOC2 by Friday (2026-04-02).
09:40 Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff.
09:45 Rajiv Menon: thanks all.
09:47 (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'K V cache' vs 'KV cache', 'Redwood Dedicate' vs 'Redwood Dedicated'). References shared: POC benchmark spreadsheet (link in follow up), POC SOW template (link in follow up), SDK repo (link in follow up).
